source_refs.note: Ovaries: a main subheading of 16.2.7 Gonads, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 67-67.

blocks.text: Ovaries secrete female sex hormones i.e., estrogen and progesterone.

items: Estrogen is secreted by Graafian follicle in response to FSH. Its functions include development of secondary sexual characteristics (e.g., breast development, widening of the pelvis, fat distribution in hips and thighs etc.), regulation of the menstrual cycle, repair of the uterine lining after menstruation, ovulation (release of an egg from ovary), maintenance of bone density, lowering "bad" cholesterol (LDL), maintenance of healthy blood pressure, regulation of mood and memory.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text: Puberty is the adolescent stage during which the sex organs mature and secondary sex characteristics appear. During puberty in males, sperm production begins, the voice deepens, the chest broadens, and hair grows on the body and face. In females, the menstrual cycle begins, the breasts grow, and the hips widen.

items: Progesterone is produced by corpus luteum in response to LH during menstrual cycle. It is also produced and released from placenta during pregnancy. It inhibits further FSH secretion from pituitary, thus preventing more follicles from ripening. It causes further thickening and vascularisation of the uterus wall for maintaining pregnancy. Progesterone suppresses ovulation.

blocks.title: For Information
blocks.text:
Small amounts of estrogen and testosterone are also released by adrenal glands.
A very small amount of testosterone is produced in females.
